sources.title: Saturn V Launch Vehicle Flight Evaluation Report, AS-506 Apollo 11 Mission, MPR-SAT-FE-69-9 / NASA-TM-X-62558
sources.publisher: NASA George C. Marshall Space Flight Center, Saturn Flight Evaluation Working Group
sources.rightsStatus: U.S. government work, public domain (NASA technical memorandum; archive.org mirror of de-indexed NTRS record)
sources.purpose: Direct source for S-IC/S-II and S-II/S-IVB physical separation METs in both Table 2-2 and the dedicated separation comparison in Table 4-3. Also provides separation evaluation narrative (Section 12) and trajectory comparison data.
sources.provenanceGrade: MIRROR — NTRS record 19900066485 de-indexed as of 2026-07-13 (API 404, citation page serves SPA shell only). Wayback Machine has only HTML wrappers (never captured PDF binary). Archive.org item saturn-v-launch-vehicle-flight-evaluation-report-as-506 hosts the PDF (11,581,879 bytes, md5 fd47020f9b289335c13c37a42731880c). Title page confirms MPR-SAT-FE-69-9, NASA-TM-X-62558, AS-506, Apollo 11 Mission, Marshall Space Flight Center. Content is U.S. government work, public domain.
sources.notes: R-016 RESOLVED. This report directly gives the S-IC/S-II separation at 162.3 sec in Table 2-2 Event 27 RANGE TIME ACTUAL and Table 4-3 ACTUAL. It directly gives the S-II/S-IVB separation at 549.0 sec in Table 2-2 Event 46 RANGE TIME ACTUAL and Table 4-3 ACTUAL. Table 2-2 TIME FROM BASE values independently cross-check those direct cells: base 161.6 + 0.7 = 162.3 and base 548.2 + 0.8 = 549.0. No independent physical-severance timestamp distinct from the command time is available. Section 12.2 confirms S-IC/S-II separation was 'accomplished as planned' with 'clean severance of the stages'. Section 12.3 confirms S-II/S-IVB separation was 'nominal'. See docs/audit/SATV-FE-SEPARATION-VERIFICATION.txt for full extraction and cross-check.

sources.title: Saturn V — NASA Science 3D Resources (GLB)
sources.rightsStatus: NASA-released visualization model — public domain; not certified flight geometry
sources.purpose: Primary 3D visualization model candidate for Saturn V / AS-506; needs inspection + semantic split before Phase 4.

inspectionSummary.childNamingPattern: Maya default (pCone, pCube, pCylinder, polySurface, groupN). No semantic S-IC/S-II/S-IVB/IU/CSM/LM labels.
inspectionSummary.verdict: Single-geometry NASA visualization model with no semantic separation. CRITICAL: Phase 3 must perform offline semantic split into S-IC, S-II, S-IVB, IU, SLA, CSM, LES via geometric/positional analysis (height ranges along Y axis, since the rocket is taller than wide). 23 embedded animations are likely deployment/rollout sequences — must be stripped before use. Units are NOT real-world meters (height 12.987 units vs Saturn V actual 110.6 m); Phase 3 normalization must scale by ~8.5x and lock Y-up.

sources.title: Apollo Lunar Module — NASA Science 3D Resources (GLB)

inspectionSummary.childNamingPattern: Maya default (group13 N, group31 N, polySurfaceN). No semantic ascent-stage / descent-stage labels.
inspectionSummary.verdict: Single-geometry NASA visualization model. CRITICAL: Phase 3 must (a) decode Draco, (b) split into ascent stage vs descent stage — likely by Y-height (ascent stage sits atop descent stage; bounds suggest split near Y=2.5), (c) verify Eagle-specific markings (American flag, plaque, 'Eagle' name, contact probes, EASEP mounting) against NASA-A11-ALSJ and NASA-LM-HB. Generic Apollo LM is NOT LM-5 by default. 135 embedded animations are likely deployment sequences — strip before use.

CSM-relevant parts: command moduel.stl (CM, 3652 tris, note original typo 'moduel' — the exact spelling 'command module.stl' does NOT exist), service module.stl (SM, 46582 tris), escape tower.stl (LES, 16030 tris), lem shroud.stl (SLA, 1162 tris).
